Status.note: A Mississippi Today article from July 31, 2026 says xAI has run trailer-mounted gas turbines at the Southaven site since August 2025 and still runs them, under a schedule to retire them by July 2027. The unit is still operating. This is the same status GEM already shows.

Planned retire.note: A Mississippi Today article from July 31, 2026 (https://mississippitoday.org/2026/07/31/southaven-xai-turbines-deadline/) reports a state order dated July 30, 2026 that sets a schedule to retire all the temporary turbines at the Southaven site. Most must stop by April 2027, and the newest ones must stop by July 14, 2027. An Action News 5 report of the same day (https://www.actionnews5.com/2026/07/31/xai-announces-fourth-data-center-turbines-be-removed-southaven-site/) says all of them will be removed and replaced by a permanent plant. I did not read the state order itself.

Status Detail.value: On July 30, 2026 the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality set a schedule to retire all 69 temporary turbines at the Southaven site. Most must stop by April 2027 and the last by July 14, 2027. xAI says a permanent power plant is replacing them.

Owner(s).note: The Mississippi air permit issued March 11, 2026 (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1834338) names MZX Tech LLC as the permit holder. The Solaris Energy Infrastructure quarterly report for June 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001697500/000162828026054349/sei-20260630.htm) also spells it MZX Tech LLC. GEM's spelling MZT Tech LLC looks like a typing error. This is a spelling fix for the same company, not a change of owner.

units.notes: Unit 1 is still running. The state order of July 30, 2026 covers 69 temporary turbines, but GEM's 495 MW counts about 27, so the capacity may be out of date. I did not find a source that gives the megawatts for all 69. The Environmental Integrity Project's Oil and Gas Watch page for the xAI Southaven Power Plant (https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/rec_d5nrijecevv1v46o78d0, read in a real browser) lists one project, the initial construction, as proposed, a simple cycle gas plant of 1,240 MW for the data center, expected in 2026. That describes the permanent plant, which is unit 2 in GEM, not the temporary turbines of unit 1.

Capacity (MW).note: The air permit issued March 11, 2026 (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1834338) lists 41 turbines: 17 Solar Titan PGM-130 sets of about 16.5 MW, 16 Solar Titan 350 sets of 35 MW and 8 ProEnergy 6000PE sets of 50 MW. That adds to 280.5 plus 560 plus 400, which is 1,240.5 MW. The permit does not print the total, so I added it myself. GEM's capacity is right.

GEM's spelling MZT Tech LLC looks like a typing error. This is a spelling fix, not a change of owner. A separate question about the leased equipment is raised in the questions list.

Status Detail.value: On March 10, 2026 the Mississippi Permit Board approved air construction permit 0680-00119 for MZX Tech LLC, covering 41 permanent turbines of 1,240.5 megawatts in total. In July 2026 xAI said it is constructing a 1.2 gigawatt plant under that permit, and news reports say supply problems have delayed the 41 turbines.

units.notes: The 41 turbines form one permitted plant at one site. I found no document that says whether they share one grid connection, because the plant is built to power the data center directly. I found no operating date for the permanent plant. Latest Activity is left alone because there was news in July 2026.

qa.recommendation: A July 2026 Mississippi Today article quotes xAI saying it is constructing a 1.2 gigawatt power plant under its air permit, which could mean unit 2 has moved from pre-construction to construction. I found no dated report of site work, turbine delivery or installation, and the same article says supply problems are delaying the 41 turbines. I did not find a second independent publisher. Please decide after one more check for site work.

qa.recommendation: The pre-construction step is best dated to August 2025, when MZX Tech LLC applied to the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality for an air construction permit on August 22, 2025. The permit was issued on March 10 to 11, 2026. The application date comes from the department's enSearch facility history for MZX Tech LLC, facility 12592.

The Permit Board approved it on March 10, 2026, per https://www.mississippifreepress.org/mississippi-permit-board-grants-xais-request-for-41-southaven-gas-turbines-to-power-memphis-data-center/.

qa.recommendation: The Solaris Energy Infrastructure quarterly report for June 2026 says Solaris holds 50.1 percent of Stateline Power LLC and MZX Tech LLC holds the other 49.9 percent. Stateline was formed in April 2025 to provide off-grid power under a long-term equipment lease to MZX Tech LLC, and it borrowed money to buy the equipment. So the leased generating equipment may be owned by Stateline, not by MZX Tech LLC. The filing does not say which turbines, how many megawatts, or whether they sit at Southaven or in Memphis. I did not change the owner. The May 2026 row on the possible-updates sheet about a change of ownership is answered this way: I found no closed sale of the plant, only this lease structure.
qa.note: Source is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001697500/000162828026054349/sei-20260630.htm. I could not open the ESG Dive story named on the sheet, and a search did not find it. The NAACP lawsuit of April 2026 covers the temporary turbines, per https://www.actionnews5.com/2026/04/14/naacp-sues-xai-alleging-unlawful-operation-gas-turbines-southaven/.

qa.recommendation: GEM shows 495 MW for 27 temporary turbines. The state order of July 30, 2026 covers 69 temporary turbines, and 46 were reported in May 2026. The megawatts for the extra turbines are not stated in any source I found. The count and capacity of unit 1 should be rechecked, though the whole group is being retired by July 2027.

The September 2026 EIA-860M table lists plant 55373, Enterprise Energy Facility, with generators CT3, CT4, CT5 and CT6, each 86.5 MW natural gas combustion turbines, operating since 2002 and retired in 2006. Its coordinates of 34.97667 and -90.03944 are about 0.6 km from GEM's point, and it appears to be the former Duke Energy plant that xAI bought, so it is the same site. The table lists the county as Clark, but the coordinates are in DeSoto County. These are the old retired turbines, not the xAI turbines, so none of the four generators matches unit 1 or unit 2. I did not report the codes as values. The old plant retired in 2006, before GEM's 2020 floor for retired units, so no record is needed.
qa.note: Source is the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx. The former Duke Energy purchase is reported at https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/elon-musks-xai-buys-former-gas-power-plant-site-in-southaven-mississippi/.
